(Currently amended) A non-transitory machine readable medium storing a program which when executed by at least one processing unit analyzes a document, the program comprising sets of instructions for: receiving a document that comprises a plurality of distinct primitive graphic elements defined separately within the document, the document having a drawing order that indicates the order in which the primitive graphic elements are displayed; calculating a first value for a first primitive graphic element and a second primitive graphic element that is subsequent to the first in the drawing order; and based on the comparison of the first value to values calculated for additional primitive graphic elements that are subsequent in the drawing order, defining a unique single structural graphic element within the document from the first and second primitive graphic elements.

(Currently amended) The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 26, wherein the first value is a specific size value.

(Currently amended) The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 26, wherein the first value represents a size corresponding to a smallest bounding box that encompasses both the first and second primitive graphic elements.

(Currently amended) The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 28, wherein the size of the smallest bounding box is calculated as a sum of a width and height of the bounding box divided by the sum of a width and height of a page containing the primitive graphic elements in their original format.

(Currently amended) The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 28, wherein the size of the smallest bounding box is calculated as an area of the bounding box divided by an area of a page containing the primitive graphic elements.

(Currently amended) The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 26, wherein the set of instructions for calculating comprises a distinct set of instructions for calculating a different value for each consecutive pair of primitive graphic elements subsequent in the drawing order, wherein the set of instructions for defining the single structural graphic element comprises sets of instructions for: utilizing the calculated values for pairs of primitive graphic elements to identify clusters of primitive graphic elements as candidates for joining as compound graphic elements; and identifying sequences of primitive graphic elements within a cluster whose bounding boxes intersect; and joining the sequences as a singular graphic element.

(Currently amended) A non-transitory machine readable medium storing a program which when executed by at least one processing unit analyzes a document, the program comprising sets of instructions for: receiving a document that comprises a plurality of distinct primitive graphic elements defined separately within the document; based on values calculated for pairs of primitive graphic elements, defining a set of consecutive primitive graphic elements as a candidate compound graphic element; using bounds of the distinct primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements within the set; and defining each distinct subset having more than one primitive graphic element as a unique single structural graphic element within the document, the structure graphic element comprising the primitive graphic elements in the distinct subset.

(Currently amended) The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 32, wherein the set of instructions for defining the set of consecutive primitive graphic elements comprises performing refined cluster analysis on the calculated values.

(Currently amended) The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 32, wherein the set of instructions for using bounds of the distinct primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements comprises sets of instructions for: selecting a first graphic element in the cluster and assigning the graphic element to a new sub-cluster; assigning a second graphic element in the cluster to the sub-cluster when a bounding box of the second graphic element overlaps a bounding box of the sub-cluster.

(Currently amended) The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 34, wherein the set of instructions for using bounds of the distinct primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements further comprises a set of instructions for assigning a third graphic element to a second sub-cluster when a bounding box of the third graphic element does not overlap the bounding box of the sub-cluster.

(Currently amended) The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 34, wherein the bounding box of the sub-cluster is determined as an intersection of the bounding boxes of all distinct primitive graphic elements already in the sub-cluster.

(Currently amended) A method for analyzing a document, the method comprising: receiving a document that comprises a plurality of distinct primitive graphic elements defined separately within the document, the document having a drawing order that indicates the order in which the primitive graphic elements are displayed; calculating a first value for a first primitive graphic element and a second primitive graphic element that is subsequent to the first in the drawing order; and based on the comparison of the first value to values calculated for additional primitive graphic elements that are subsequent in the drawing order, defining a unique single structural graphic element within the document from the first and second primitive graphic elements.

(Currently amended) The method of claim 37, wherein the first value represents a size corresponding to a smallest bounding box that encompasses both the first and second primitive graphic elements.

(Currently amended) The method of claim 38, wherein the size of the smallest bounding box is calculated as a sum of a width and height of the bounding box divided by a sum of a width and height of a page containing the primitive graphic elements in their original format.

(Currently amended) The method of claim 38, wherein the size of the smallest bounding box is calculated as an area of the bounding box divided by an area of a page containing the primitive graphic elements.

(Currently amended) The method of claim 37, wherein the calculating comprises calculating a distinct value for each pair of consecutive primitive graphic elements subsequent in the drawing order, wherein defining the single structural graphic element comprises: utilizing the calculated values for pairs of primitive graphic elements to identify clusters of primitive graphic elements as candidates for joining as compound graphic elements; and identifying sequences of primitive graphic elements within a cluster whose bounding boxes intersect; and joining the sequences as singular graphic elements.

(Currently amended) An apparatus comprising: a set of processing units; and a machine readable medium storing a program which when executed by at least one processing unit analyzes a document, the program comprising sets of instructions for: receiving a document that comprises a plurality of distinct primitive graphic elements defined separately within the document; based on values calculated for pairs of distinct primitive graphic elements, defining a set of consecutive primitive graphic elements as a candidate compound graphic element; using bounds of the distinct primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements within the set; and defining each distinct subset having more than one primitive graphic element as a unique single structural graphic element within the document, the structure graphic element comprising the distinct primitive graphic elements in the particular subset.

(Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 42, wherein the set of instructions for using bounds of the distinct primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements comprises sets of instructions for: selecting a first graphic element in the cluster and assigning the graphic element to a new sub-cluster; assigning a second graphic element in the cluster to the sub-cluster when a bounding box of the second graphic element overlaps a bounding box of the sub-cluster.

(Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 43, wherein the set of instructions for using bounds of the distinct primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements further comprises a set of instructions for assigning a third graphic element to a second sub-cluster when a bounding box of the third graphic element does not overlap the bounding box of the sub-cluster.

(Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 43, wherein the bounding box of the sub-cluster is determined as an intersection of the bounding boxes of all distinct primitive graphic elements already in the sub-cluster.

(Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 42, wherein the document comprises an unstructured vector graphics document containing a structured representation of the primitive graphic elements.
